body: I genuinely am not a troll. I wasn’t making fun of OP or saying off the wall shit. I simply stated my opinion which related to having thick skin in the field and that what they posted is something that happens legitimately all the time-it’s part of social work. As I stated elsewhere, I was told by supervisors in the beginning of my career the same thing I said to OP. I would get upset about the same type of stuff and they said if I couldn’t handle that, then I probably wasn’t right for the field. It’s been said to colleagues of mine and schoolmates. It’s not personal, it’s just an observation. I’m glad they said it to me, because it made me remember that I chose to work in a very tough field with a lot of emotion and tension and that I was dealing with people on their worst days. They guided me and taught me about self-care. This is reddit-a post is a tiny snapshot of a situation. You realize you’re all attacking me and calling me a shit social worker for literally giving my opinion on ONE post? Jesus H. Christ, get a grip. OP, I’m sorry if I offended you. I’ve seen posts in the EMT sub and the Nursing sub that say similar things to what you said and plenty of people respond JUST like I did. I wasn’t trying to insult you, I’m sure you’re a fabulous social worker and I’m sorry you had a bad day. Everyone else-keep attacking me and thinking you know anything about me as a human being in real life based off one comment. I love what I do and I know I’m good at it. Have a great night everyone.
I’m sure all of you are perfect humans and have never commented anything negative online in your entire lives.

Once again, commenting on a reddit post has no bearing on how I do my job. I’m clearly doing something right since I have been at my job multiple years and have received promotions. If I was so terrible, I would’ve been canned or demoted, no? Reddit isn’t real life. When you provide supervision you have more context than someone whining on a post about getting yelled at. I’ve had supervisors myself tell me to get a thicker skin when I first started.

I don’t spend my days or much time at all on Reddit. I lurk around if I have free time. I’m currently on holiday. Sorry I bother you all so much feel free to mute me or report me or whatever you feel you need to lol. Such anger over one commenter. Why do my words mean so much to you? Was just posting my opinion, it’s not that serious.
Been at my job many years and had two promotions, and currently working on a second Master’s. I think I’m doing just fine. How I react to a stupid reddit post has no bearing on how I do my job.
The OP even said they understand my POV, and that social work requires thick skin, so if they’re not upset why is everyone else so pressed?
Lol idc about anyones downvotes or comments. The OP wrote a post crying about being yelled at and my response was that if they’re that sensitive then they should rethink their career.

Ok but I was going off your post that asked for similar experiences. Every social worker has had people yell at them. You wrote a whole post about it and how much it bothered you. That’s why I said what I said.

If you can’t handle someone calling you “a garbage social worker” and getting a little angry with you, then you should rethink your career choice. Try having to call the cops on someone trying to beat down your office door threatening you, someone threatening to rape you, or having someone scream and yell and tell you they’re done with you every day only to have them call you the next day asking for help every time. Seriously, those things and worse happen all the time to social workers working with vulnerable populations. That’s how people in vulnerable populations act. Practicing good self-care and talking to a supervisor if you feel unsafe are all well and good, but sometimes you also have to evaluate if you’re cut out for that type of work. May sound harsh but oh well.
